lessons.learning_objectives: Use basic greetings and farewells appropriately.
lessons.targe_language: hola, adiós, buenos días, buenas tardes, buenas noches
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] ¡Hola! Welcome! Today you'll learn basic greetings to start and end conversations in Spanish.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] To say "hello", use "¡Hola!". To say "goodbye", use "¡Adiós!". The 'H' is always silent!

[Bubble Type: Example] ¡Hola, buenos días! (Hello, good morning!)
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "Hello"

[Target answer: ¡Hola!]

[Explanation: ¡Hola means Hello and the letter H is silent.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "¡_____, nos vemos!"

[Target answer: Adiós]

[Explanation: Adiós is the standard way to say goodbye.]

[Item 3: Multiple Choice] Good morning: A) Buenas noches B) Buenos días C) Buenas tardes

[Target answer: B) Buenos días]

[Explanation: Buenos días translates to good morning.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Ask and give your name.
lessons.targe_language: me llamo, ¿cómo te llamas?, mucho gusto
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Welcome! Today you will learn how to ask someone's name and introduce yourself.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Ask "What's your name?" with "¿Cómo te llamas?". Answer "My name is..." with "Me llamo [name]".

[Bubble Type: Example] — ¿Cómo te llamas? — Me llamo Carlos.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "My name is Juan"

[Target answer: Me llamo Juan.]

[Explanation: Me llamo is used for My name is.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "¿Cómo _____ llamas?"

[Target answer: te]

[Explanation: te goes with llamas when asking someone informally.]

[Item 3: Dialogue Completion] Complete: "— ¿Cómo te llamas? — _____, mucho gusto."

[Target answer: Me llamo Maria]

[Explanation: Use Me llamo followed by your name.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Introduce yourself using the verb ser.
lessons.targe_language: soy, eres, es, nombre
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Hi there! Today you'll learn how to say "I am..." using the Spanish verb "ser".

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Use "Yo soy" to say "I am". You can also drop "yo" and just say "Soy".

[Bubble Type: Example] Yo soy Ana. / Soy estudiante.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Sentence Building] Arrange: "soy / Yo / Elena"

[Target answer: Yo soy Elena]

[Explanation: Yo soy means I am.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "Yo _____ profesor."

[Target answer: soy]

[Explanation: soy is the 'I am' form of ser.]

[Item 3: Multiple Choice] How do you say "I am"? A) Yo eres B) Yo soy C) Yo es

[Target answer: B) Yo soy]

[Explanation: Yo always pairs with soy.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Ask how someone is and respond.
lessons.targe_language: estoy bien, estoy mal, más o menos, ¿y tú?
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Let's learn how to ask "How are you?" and express how you feel today.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Ask "¿Cómo estás?". Reply with "Estoy bien" (I'm well) or "Estoy mal" (I'm doing bad).

[Bubble Type: Example] — ¿Cómo estás? — Estoy bien, ¿y tú?
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "I am well"

[Target answer: Estoy bien]

[Explanation: Estoy bien means I am well.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "— ¿Cómo estás? — Estoy _____, gracias." (so-so)

[Target answer: más o menos]

[Explanation: más o menos means so-so or okay.]

[Item 3: Natural Reply] Reply to "¿Cómo estás?":

[Target answer: Estoy bien, ¿y tú?]

[Explanation: Always ask ¿y tú? back to be polite.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Combine greetings, names, and ser/estar in a short exchange.
lessons.targe_language: review of module vocabulary
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Welcome to the Unit 1 Review! Let me test everything you've learned so far.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Remember: "Me llamo" / "Soy" for identity, and "Estoy" for feelings.

[Bubble Type: Example] ¡Hola! Me llamo Pedro, soy profesor. ¿Cómo estás?
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Multiple Choice] Greeting for 8 AM: A) Buenas noches B) Buenos días C) Buenas tardes

[Target answer: B) Buenos días]

[Explanation: Buenos días is used in the morning.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "¡Hola! Yo _____ Ana y _____ bien."

[Target answer: soy, estoy]

[Explanation: Use soy for identity and estoy for feelings.]

[Item 3: Dialogue Completion] Finish dialogue: "— ¡Hola! ¿Cómo te llamas? — _____"

[Target answer: Me llamo Maria]

[Explanation: State your name using Me llamo or Soy.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Ask and state country of origin.
lessons.targe_language: ¿de dónde eres?, soy de, país, ciudad
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Today you will learn how to ask people where they are from in Spanish!

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Ask "¿De dónde eres?" (Where are you from?). Answer "Soy de [Country]" (I am from...).

[Bubble Type: Example] — ¿De dónde eres? — Soy de España.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "Where are you from?"

[Target answer: ¿De dónde eres?]

[Explanation: ¿De dónde eres? asks for origin.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "Yo soy _____ México."

[Target answer: de]

[Explanation: Use 'de' after soy to specify origin country.]

[Item 3: Multiple Choice] How do you say "I am from Vietnam"? A) Soy Vietnam B) Soy de Vietnam C) De soy Vietnam

[Target answer: B) Soy de Vietnam]

[Explanation: Soy de is required before place names.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Describe nationality with correct gender agreement.
lessons.targe_language: mexicano, mexicana, español, española
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Learn how to express your nationality with gender agreement in Spanish.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Adjectives ending in -o change to -a for females: "mexicano" (male), "mexicana" (female).

[Bubble Type: Example] Él es mexicano. Ella es mexicana.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Fill in the blank] "Maria es _____ (Spanish)."

[Target answer: española]

[Explanation: Use feminine form española for Maria.]

[Item 2: Sentence Building] Arrange: "es / Carlos / mexicano"

[Target answer: Carlos es mexicano]

[Explanation: Carlos is masculine so use mexicano.]

[Item 3: Translation] Translate "I am Spanish (female)"

[Target answer: Soy española]

[Explanation: Female speaker uses española.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Talk about languages you speak.
lessons.targe_language: hablo, hablas, español, inglés, vietnamita
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Let's learn how to talk about languages you speak using the verb "hablar".

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Say "Hablo..." for "I speak". Ask "¿Hablas...?" for "Do you speak...?".

[Bubble Type: Example] Hablo español e inglés.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "I speak Spanish"

[Target answer: Hablo español]

[Explanation: Hablo means I speak.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "¿_____ inglés?" (Do you speak...)

[Target answer: Hablas]

[Explanation: Hablas is the 'you' form of hablar.]

[Item 3: Multiple Choice] "I speak English": A) Hablas inglés B) Hablo inglés C) Habla inglés

[Target answer: B) Hablo inglés]

[Explanation: Hablo pairs with I/Yo.]

lessons.learning_objectives: State where you live currently.
lessons.targe_language: vivo, vives, en, ciudad, capital
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Today you'll learn to express where you live using the verb "vivir".

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Say "Vivo en [city/country]" for "I live in...". Ask "¿Dónde vives?" for "Where do you live?".

[Bubble Type: Example] Vivo en Madrid, España.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Fill in the blank] "Yo _____ en Barcelona."

[Target answer: vivo]

[Explanation: Vivo is the 'I live' form of vivir.]

[Item 2: Translation] Translate "Where do you live?"

[Target answer: ¿Dónde vives?]

[Explanation: ¿Dónde vives? asks for living location.]

[Item 3: Sentence Building] Arrange: "vives / ¿Dónde / tú ?"

[Target answer: ¿Dónde vives tú?]

[Explanation: Standard order for asking where you live.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Combine origin, nationality, language, and residence.
lessons.targe_language: review of unit 2 vocabulary
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Welcome to Unit 2 Review! Let's combine origin, languages, and residence.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Remember: "Soy de" = origin, "Vivo en" = location, "Hablo" = language.

[Bubble Type: Example] Soy de Vietnam, vivo en Hanói y hablo vietnamita.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Fill in the blank] "Soy _____ México, pero vivo _____ España."

[Target answer: de, en]

[Explanation: Soy de for origin, vivo en for residence.]

[Item 2: Multiple Choice] "I speak Spanish": A) Vivo español B) Hablo español C) Soy español

[Target answer: B) Hablo español]

[Explanation: Hablo is used for speaking languages.]

[Item 3: Dialogue Completion] Complete: "— ¿De dónde eres? — _____"

[Target answer: Soy de Vietnam]

[Explanation: Answer with Soy de + country.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Talk about family members using possessive adjectives.
lessons.targe_language: padre, madre, hermano, hermana, mi, tu
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Let's learn basic family words and how to say "my" or "your" in Spanish.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Use "mi" for "my" and "tu" for "your". Example: "mi padre" (my father), "tu madre" (your mother).

[Bubble Type: Example] Mi hermano se llama Luis.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "My mother"

[Target answer: Mi madre]

[Explanation: Mi means my.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "_____ hermano es profesor." (My...)

[Target answer: Mi]

[Explanation: Mi is the possessive adjective for my.]

[Item 3: Multiple Choice] How do you say "Your father"? A) Su padre B) Mi padre C) Tu padre

[Target answer: C) Tu padre]

[Explanation: Tu means your (informal).]

lessons.learning_objectives: Express family members you have using tener.
lessons.targe_language: tengo, tienes, un, una, dos, tres
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Today you will learn how to say what family members you have using "tener".

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Use "Tengo..." to say "I have...". Use "un" (masculine) and "una" (feminine) for "a/one".

[Bubble Type: Example] Tengo un hermano y una hermana.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "I have a sister"

[Target answer: Tengo una hermana]

[Explanation: Tengo means I have, una is feminine singular.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "¿_____ hermanos tú?" (Do you have...)

[Target answer: Tienes]

[Explanation: Tienes is the 'you' form of tener.]

[Item 3: Sentence Building] Arrange: "hermanos / dos / Tengo"

[Target answer: Tengo dos hermanos]

[Explanation: Verb + number + noun structure.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Ask and state age in Spanish.
lessons.targe_language: años, ¿cuántos años tienes?, tengo... años
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] In Spanish, you "have" years instead of "being" years old! Let's learn how to express age.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Ask "¿Cuántos años tienes?". Answer "Tengo [number] años" (I am ... years old).

[Bubble Type: Example] — ¿Cuántos años tienes? — Tengo 25 años.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "How old are you?"

[Target answer: ¿Cuántos años tienes?]

[Explanation: Spanish uses tener (to have) for age.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "Yo _____ veinte años."

[Target answer: tengo]

[Explanation: Tengo expresses age in Spanish.]

[Item 3: Multiple Choice] How to say "I am 30 years old"? A) Soy 30 años B) Estoy 30 años C) Tengo 30 años

[Target answer: C) Tengo 30 años]

[Explanation: Never use ser/estar for age in Spanish.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Describe pets and family members with adjectives.
lessons.targe_language: grande, pequeño, perro, gato, bonito, alto
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Learn how to describe your pets or family members using simple adjectives.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Adjectives match gender/number: "grande" (big), "pequeño/a" (small), "bonito/a" (pretty).

[Bubble Type: Example] Mi perro es grande. Mi gata es pequeña.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "My dog is big"

[Target answer: Mi perro es grande]

[Explanation: Mi perro = my dog, es grande = is big.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "Mi gata es _____ (small)."

[Target answer: pequeña]

[Explanation: Feminine form pequeña matches gata.]

[Item 3: Sentence Building] Arrange: "bonito / Mi / es / gato"

[Target answer: Mi gato es bonito]

[Explanation: Subject + verb + adjective order.]

lessons.lesson_name: Repaso: Mi familia y bạn bè
lessons.learning_objectives: Talk about family, age, and pets in a unified conversation.
lessons.targe_language: review of unit 3 vocabulary
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Welcome to Unit 3 Review! Let's test your ability to talk about family and age.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Remember: Use "mi/tu" for possession and "tengo" for age and family count.

[Bubble Type: Example] Tengo 30 años, mi hermano tiene 20 años y tenemos un perro grande.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Fill in the blank] "Tengo 20 _____ y _____ un hermano."

[Target answer: años, tengo]

[Explanation: años for age, tengo for I have.]

[Item 2: Multiple Choice] "I am 20 years old": A) Soy 20 años B) Tengo 20 años C) Estoy 20 años

[Target answer: B) Tengo 20 años]

[Explanation: Always use tener for age.]

[Item 3: Dialogue Completion] Complete: "— ¿Cuántos años tienes? — _____"

[Target answer: Tengo 20 años]

[Explanation: Answer with Tengo + number + años.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Ask and tell the time.
lessons.targe_language: ¿qué hora es?, es la una, son las dos/tres, en punto
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Welcome to Unit 4! Today you'll learn how to ask and tell the time in Spanish.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Ask "¿Qué hora es?". Use "Es la una" for 1:00, and "Son las..." for other hours (e.g., "Son las dos").

[Bubble Type: Example] — ¿Qué hora es? — Son las tres en punto.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "What time is it?"

[Target answer: ¿Qué hora es?]

[Explanation: ¿Qué hora es? is the standard phrase for asking the time.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "_____ la una." (It is 1:00)

[Target answer: Es]

[Explanation: Use Es (singular) only for 1:00.]

[Item 3: Multiple Choice] How do you say "It is 4:00"? A) Es las cuatro B) Son las cuatro C) Tengo las cuatro

[Target answer: B) Son las cuatro]

[Explanation: Use Son las for numbers from 2 to 12.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Express basic daily morning habits using reflexive verbs.
lessons.targe_language: me levanto, me ducho, me lavo, temprano
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Today you'll learn to describe your morning routines using reflexive actions.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Reflexive actions use "me" for "I": "Me levanto" (I get up), "Me ducho" (I shower). Use "a las [time]" for time.

[Bubble Type: Example] Me levanto a las siete de la mañana.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "I get up at 7"

[Target answer: Me levanto a las siete]

[Explanation: Me levanto means I get up, a las specifies time.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "Yo _____ ducho a las ocho."

[Target answer: me]

[Explanation: Reflexive pronoun 'me' matches 'yo'.]

[Item 3: Sentence Building] Arrange: "las / a / Me / levanto / seis"

[Target answer: Me levanto a las seis]

[Explanation: Action + time preposition 'a las' + number.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Talk about meals and meal times.
lessons.targe_language: desayuno, como, ceno, el desayuno, la cena
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Let's learn how to talk about your meal schedules during the day.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Use "Desayuno" (I eat breakfast), "Como" (I eat lunch), and "Ceno" (I eat dinner).

[Bubble Type: Example] Desayuno a las ocho y ceno a las nueve.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "I eat breakfast"

[Target answer: Desayuno]

[Explanation: Desayuno means I eat breakfast in Spanish.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "Yo _____ (eat dinner) a las nueve."

[Target answer: ceno]

[Explanation: Ceno comes from the verb cenar.]

[Item 3: Multiple Choice] "I eat lunch at 1:00": A) Como a la una B) Desayuno a la una C) Ceno a la una

[Target answer: A) Como a la una]

[Explanation: Comer/Como refers to eating lunch/meal.]

lessons.learning_objectives: State the days you work or study.
lessons.targe_language: lunes, martes, miércoles, jueves, viernes, sábado, domingo
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Learn the days of the week and how to state your daily schedule.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Days of the week in Spanish are not capitalized! Use "de [day] a [day]" for "from [day] to [day]".

[Bubble Type: Example] Trabajo de lunes a viernes.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "from Monday to Friday"

[Target answer: de lunes a viernes]

[Explanation: de... a... means from... to...]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "No trabajo los _____." (Saturdays)

[Target answer: sábados]

[Explanation: Use plural 'los sábados' for on Saturdays.]

[Item 3: Multiple Choice] Which word means "Monday"? A) Martes B) Lunes C) Viernes

[Target answer: B) Lunes]

[Explanation: Lunes is Monday.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Describe your typical weekday schedule from morning to night.
lessons.targe_language: review of routine vocabulary
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Welcome to the Unit 4 Review! Let's combine time, routine verbs, and days of the week.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Remember: Use "a las..." for specific times and "de... a..." for ranges.

[Bubble Type: Example] De lunes a viernes, me levanto a las seis y trabajo a las ocho.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Fill in the blank] "Me levanto _____ las siete y _____ (eat breakfast) a las ocho."

[Target answer: a, desayuno]

[Explanation: 'a las' for time, 'desayuno' for eating breakfast.]

[Item 2: Multiple Choice] "It is 8:00": A) Es las ocho B) Son las ocho C) A las ocho

[Target answer: B) Son las ocho]

[Explanation: Son las is used for plural hours.]

[Item 3: Dialogue Completion] Complete: "— ¿A qué hora desayunas? — _____"

[Target answer: Desayuno a las ocho]

[Explanation: Action + a las + hour.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Express hunger and thirst using tener.
lessons.targe_language: tengo hambre, tengo sed, agua, comida
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Today you'll learn how to say you are hungry or thirsty in Spanish using "tener".

[Bubble Type: Teaching] In Spanish, you say "I have hunger" ("Tengo hambre") and "I have thirst" ("Tengo sed").

[Bubble Type: Example] Tengo hambre. ¿Hay un restaurante cerca?
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "I am thirsty"

[Target answer: Tengo sed]

[Explanation: Spanish uses tener (to have) + sed for thirst.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "Yo _____ hambre, quiero comer."

[Target answer: tengo]

[Explanation: Tengo pairs with I/Yo.]

[Item 3: Multiple Choice] How do you say "I am hungry"? A) Estoy hambre B) Tengo hambre C) Soy hambre

[Target answer: B) Tengo hambre]

[Explanation: Never use ser/estar for hunger or thirst.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Order food and drinks politely in a cafe.
lessons.targe_language: quiero, por favor, café, té, agua, pan, gracias
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Learn how to order basic food and drinks at a cafe in Spanish.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Use "Un [item], por favor" or "Quiero [item]" to make a polite order.

[Bubble Type: Example] Un café con leche, por favor.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "A coffee, please"

[Target answer: Un café, por favor]

[Explanation: Un café = A coffee, por favor = please.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "_____ una cerveza, por favor." (I want)

[Target answer: Quiero]

[Explanation: Quiero means I want.]

[Item 3: Dialogue Completion] Complete: "— ¿Qué desea? — _____, por favor." (A water)

[Target answer: Un agua / Una botella de agua]

[Explanation: Express request with article + noun + por favor.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Ask how much something costs and understand basic numbers.
lessons.targe_language: ¿cuánto cuesta?, euro, euros, cuenta, la cuenta
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Today you'll learn how to ask for prices and request the bill.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Ask "¿Cuánto cuesta?" (How much does it cost?) and "La cuenta, por favor" (The bill, please).

[Bubble Type: Example] —¿Cuánto cuesta el café? —Son tres euros.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "How much does it cost?"

[Target answer: ¿Cuánto cuesta?]

[Explanation: ¿Cuánto cuesta? is used for prices.]

[Item 2: Translation] Translate "The bill, please"

[Target answer: La cuenta, por favor]

[Explanation: La cuenta means the bill/check.]

[Item 3: Fill in the blank] "¿Cuánto _____ el agua?"

[Target answer: cuesta]

[Explanation: Cuesta matches singular items.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Express likes and dislikes regarding food.
lessons.targe_language: me gusta, no me gusta, el café, el té, la fruta
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Let's learn how to express what foods and drinks you like or dislike.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Use "Me gusta [singular item]" for "I like...". Add "No" at the front for dislikes: "No me gusta...".

[Bubble Type: Example] Me gusta el café, pero no me gusta el té.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "I like coffee"

[Target answer: Me gusta el café]

[Explanation: Me gusta + definite article + noun.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "No _____ gusta la cerveza."

[Target answer: me]

[Explanation: 'me' pronoun indicates 'to me' in gustar.]

[Item 3: Sentence Building] Arrange: "gusta / el / Me / té"

[Target answer: Me gusta el té]

[Explanation: Structure: Me + gusta + article + noun.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Roleplay ordering a meal, asking for the price, and expressing taste.
lessons.targe_language: review of food vocabulary
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Welcome to Unit 5 Review! Let's practice ordering food and drinks in a restaurant scenario.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Remember: Use "Quiero..." or "...por favor" to order, and "¿Cuánto cuesta?" for price.

[Bubble Type: Example] Tengo hambre. Quiero una pizza, por favor. ¿Cuánto cuesta?
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Multiple Choice] How to ask for the bill: A) La cuenta, por favor B) Tengo hambre C) Me gusta la cuenta

[Target answer: A) La cuenta, por favor]

[Explanation: La cuenta, por favor requests the bill.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "Tengo _____, quiero un café, por _____"

[Target answer: sed, favor]

[Explanation: Tengo sed = I'm thirsty, por favor = please.]

[Item 3: Natural Reply] Reply to waiter "¿Qué desea?":

[Target answer: Un café, por favor / Quiero un café]

[Explanation: State item + por favor.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Inquire about clothing items using demonstrative adjectives.
lessons.targe_language: camiseta, pantalones, zapatos, este, esta
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Welcome to Unit 6! Today you'll learn how to point out and ask for specific items while shopping.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Use "este" for masculine items ("este pantalón") and "esta" for feminine items ("esta camiseta").

[Bubble Type: Example] ¿Tienes esta camiseta en rojo?
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "this shirt"

[Target answer: esta camiseta]

[Explanation: Camiseta is feminine singular, so use esta.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "Quiero _____ pantalón." (this)

[Target answer: este]

[Explanation: Pantalón is masculine singular, so use este.]

[Item 3: Multiple Choice] Choose "this jacket (la chaqueta)": A) Este chaqueta B) Esta chaqueta C) Estos chaqueta

[Target answer: B) Esta chaqueta]

[Explanation: Chaqueta is feminine, requires esta.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Describe the color of clothes with proper gender/number agreement.
lessons.targe_language: rojo, roja, azul, negro, negra, blanco, blanca
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Learn how to describe clothing colors and match them to the item's gender.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Colors ending in -o change to -a for feminine items: "camisa roja". Colors like "azul" don't change!

[Bubble Type: Example] El abrigo es negro y la camisa es blanca.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Fill in the blank] "La camiseta es _____ (red)."

[Target answer: roja]

[Explanation: Camiseta is feminine, so rojo becomes roja.]

[Item 2: Translation] Translate "The black shoe"

lessons.learning_objectives: Talk about sizes and fitting of clothes.

lessons.learning_objectives: Describe what you or someone else is wearing.

lessons.learning_objectives: Combine asking for clothes, colors, sizes, and prices in a shopping scenario.
lessons.targe_language: review of shopping vocabulary

lessons.learning_objectives: Ask for and express the location of places in a city.
lessons.targe_language: ¿dónde está?, está en, el banco, el hotel, el museo
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Welcome to Unit 7! Today you'll learn how to ask where places are located in a city.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Ask "¿Dónde está [place]?" (Where is...?). Answer "Está en..." (It is in/at...).

lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "Where is the hotel?"

[Target answer: ¿Dónde está el hotel?]

[Explanation: ¿Dónde está asks for location of singular places.]

[Target answer: está]

[Explanation: Use 'está' for location of singular items.]

[Item 3: Multiple Choice] How to ask "Where is the restaurant?": A) ¿Dónde es el restaurante? B) ¿Dónde está el restaurante? C) ¿Dónde hay el restaurante?

[Explanation: Always use estar for physical location.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Express whether a place is near or far.
lessons.targe_language: cerca, lejos, cerca de, lejos de

lessons.phase_2:

[Explanation: Cerca means near/close.]

[Explanation: Use 'de' after lejos/cerca when specifying a reference place.]

[Item 3: Sentence Building] Arrange: "la / cerca / Está / estación / de"

lessons.learning_objectives: Give and understand simple directional instructions.
lessons.targe_language: gira, sigue, a la derecha, a la izquierda, recto

lessons.phase_2:

[Explanation: Sigue recto means continue straight ahead.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Talk about modes of transportation you use.
lessons.targe_language: voy, vas, va, en autobús, en tren, en metro, a pie

lessons.learning_objectives: Practice asking for locations, directions, and transportation in a city context.
lessons.targe_language: review of city vocabulary
lessons.phase_1:

lessons.learning_objectives: Ask strangers how to reach a specific landmark.

[Target answer: B) ¿Cómo llego al hotel?]

[Explanation: Use ¿Cómo llego a...? Note: a + el = al.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Inquire about and state the existence of services nearby.

[Explanation: Always use Hay to express existence.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Describe spatial relation using relative prepositions.

lessons.learning_objectives: Describe what exists in your neighborhood using hay and adjectives.

lessons.learning_objectives: Purchase train or bus tickets with destination and class options.

lessons.learning_objectives: Describe current weather conditions using hacer and estar.

lessons.learning_objectives: Talk about weather in different seasons and preferred activities.

lessons.phase_1:

[Explanation: Time phrase + weather verb + weather noun.]

[Explanation: Fue is the 3rd person singular past of ir.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Describe past background weather conditions using the imperfect tense.
lessons.targe_language: hacía buen tiempo, hacía frío, llovía, cuando
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Learn how to set the scene by describing past weather using the Imperfect tense ("hacía").

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Use "hacía [weather]" for ongoing past weather: "hacía buen tiempo" (the weather was good).

[Bubble Type: Example] Cuando fui a Madrid, hacía mucho sol.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "The weather was good"

[Target answer: Hacía buen tiempo]

[Explanation: Hacía is the imperfect form for past weather.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "Ayer _____ (it was cold) cuando salí."

[Target answer: hacía frío]

[Explanation: Hacía frío describes ongoing past weather background.]

[Item 3: Sentence Building] Arrange: "tiempo / Hacía / buen / ayer"

[Target answer: Hacía buen tiempo ayer]

[Explanation: Weather verb + descriptor + time adverb.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Talk about childhood habits and descriptions using "era".
lessons.targe_language: cuando era niño/a, era, eras, pequeño/a, siempre
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Today you'll learn to talk about your childhood using "cuando era niño/a" (when I was a child).

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Use "era" (I/he/she was) to describe who or how you were in childhood: "Cuando era niño, era tímido".

[Bubble Type: Example] Cuando era pequeña, vivía en un pueblo muy bonito.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "When I was a child (male)"

[Target answer: Cuando era niño]

[Explanation: Era comes from ser, used for past states/childhood.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "Cuando _____ niña, jugaba en el parque." (I was)

[Target answer: era]

[Explanation: Era matches 'yo' in the imperfect tense.]

[Item 3: Multiple Choice] Choose "When he was young": A) Cuando era joven B) Cuando fui joven C) Cuando estuve joven

[Target answer: A) Cuando era joven]

[Explanation: Use era (imperfect of ser) for past age/stages.]

lessons.lesson_name: Iba al parque todos los días
lessons.learning_objectives: Describe repeated past habits and routines using "iba".
lessons.targe_language: iba, ibas, todos los días, siempre, a menudo
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Learn how to express past repeated habits using the imperfect tense of ir ("iba").

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Use "iba" (I/he/she used to go) with habit expressions like "todos los días" (every day).

[Bubble Type: Example] Cuando era niño, iba al parque todos los días.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "I used to go to the park"

[Target answer: Iba al parque]

[Explanation: Iba expresses habitual past movement.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "Mi hermano _____ (used to go) a la escuela en autobús."

[Target answer: iba]

[Explanation: Iba is the imperfect form of ir.]

[Item 3: Dialogue Completion] Complete: "— ¿Qué hacías de niño? — _____"

[Target answer: Iba al parque todos los días / Jugaba mucho]

[Explanation: Describe a habitual past activity.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Narrate short memories combining preterite (events) and imperfect (background).
lessons.targe_language: review of past tenses vocabulary
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Welcome to Unit 7 Review! Practice combining background descriptions (era/hacía) with past events.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Remember: Use "era/hacía/iba" for background & habits, and "estuve/fui/hice" for specific events.

[Bubble Type: Example] Cuando era niño, hacía calor en verano y siempre iba a la playa.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Fill in the blank] "Cuando _____ (I was) niño, _____ (the weather was good)."

[Target answer: era, hacía buen tiempo]

[Explanation: era for childhood description, hacía for weather.]

[Item 2: Multiple Choice] Describe a specific past illness: A) Estuve enfermo la semana pasada B) Era enfermo la semana pasada C) Iba enfermo la semana pasada

[Target answer: A) Estuve enfermo la semana pasada]

[Explanation: Preterite estuve for specific past duration.]

[Item 3: Dialogue Completion] Complete: "— ¿Adónde ibas en verano? — _____"

[Target answer: Iba a la playa / Iba al pueblo de mis tíos]

[Explanation: Express past habitual destination with iba.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Express hobbies and free time preferences using gustar + verbs.
lessons.targe_language: me gusta, te gusta, escuchar música, ver películas, leer, hacer deporte
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Welcome to Unit 8! Today you'll learn how to talk about your favorite hobbies and interests.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Use "Me gusta + [infinitive verb]" (e.g., "Me gusta leer", "Me gusta escuchar música").

[Bubble Type: Example] En mi tiempo libre me gusta ver películas y hacer deporte.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "I like to listen to music"

[Target answer: Me gusta escuchar música]

[Explanation: Me gusta + infinitive verb.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "¿Qué _____ gusta hacer en tu tiempo libre?" (you informal)

[Target answer: te]

[Explanation: 'te' pronoun matches informal 'you'.]

[Item 3: Multiple Choice] "I like to read": A) Me gusta leer B) Me gusto leer C) Yo me gusta leer

[Target answer: A) Me gusta leer]

[Explanation: Me gusta takes an infinitive verb like leer.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Express strong interests using interesar and encantar.
lessons.targe_language: me encanta, me interesa, fascinar, el arte, la historia
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Learn how to use "encantar" (love) and "interesar" (be interested in) for hobbies.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] "Me encanta" = I love doing/item; "Me interesa" = I am interested in...

[Bubble Type: Example] Me encanta el arte y me interesa la historia.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "I love music"

[Target answer: Me encanta la música]

[Explanation: Encantar means to love something passionately.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "Me _____ la historia española." (interests)

[Target answer: interesa]

[Explanation: Interesa pairs with singular nouns like la historia.]

[Item 3: Sentence Building] Arrange: "encanta / viajar / Me / mucho"

[Target answer: Me encanta viajar mucho]

[Explanation: Pronoun + verb + infinitive + adverb.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Give opinions on clothing fit and style using "quedar".
lessons.targe_language: te queda bien, te queda mal, te queda grande/pequeño, probarse, probador
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Learn how to express how clothes fit someone using the verb "quedar".

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Use "Te queda bien" (It suits/fits you well) or "Te queda grande" (It's too big for you).

[Bubble Type: Example] Esta camisa te queda muy bien. ¿Dónde está el probador?
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "This shirt fits you well"

[Target answer: Esta camisa te queda bien]

[Explanation: Queda expresses how an item fits or looks.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "Estos pantalones te _____ grandes." (fit)

[Target answer: quedan]

[Explanation: Plural noun 'pantalones' requires plural 'quedan'.]

[Item 3: Multiple Choice] How to say "Where is the fitting room?": A) ¿Dónde está el probador? B) ¿Dónde queda la tienda? C) ¿Cuánto cuesta la camisa?

[Target answer: A) ¿Dónde está el probador?]

[Explanation: El probador = fitting room.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Politely negotiate prices at traditional markets using "Poder".
lessons.targe_language: ¿puede bajar el precio?, descuento, oferta, barato, caro
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Learn polite phrases to negotiate prices at open-air markets in Spanish-speaking countries.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Ask "¿Puede bajar el precio?" (Can you lower the price?) or "¿Tiene algún descuento?".

[Bubble Type: Example] Es un poco caro. ¿Puede bajar el precio o hacerme un descuento?
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "Can you lower the price?"

[Target answer: ¿Puede bajar el precio?]

[Explanation: Bajar el precio means to lower the price.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "¿Tiene alguna _____ en esta tienda?" (discount/offer)

[Target answer: oferta]

[Explanation: Oferta means special offer or sale.]

[Item 3: Multiple Choice] "It is very expensive": A) Es muy barato B) Es muy caro C) Es muy grande

[Target answer: B) Es muy caro]

[Explanation: Caro means expensive.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Roleplay choosing products, checking fit, and bargaining for the best deal.
lessons.targe_language: review of shopping & hobbies vocabulary
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Welcome to Unit 8 Review! Let's practice discussing hobbies, fitting clothes, and market shopping.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Remember: "Me encanta...", "Te queda bien...", and "¿Puede bajar el precio?" for negotiations.

[Bubble Type: Example] Me encanta esta chaqueta, pero es cara. ¿Puede bajar el precio?
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Fill in the blank] "Esta falda te _____ bien, pero es un poco _____ (expensive)."

[Target answer: queda, cara]

[Explanation: queda for fit, cara for expensive.]

[Item 2: Multiple Choice] Express loving to read: A) Me gusta leer B) Me encanta leer C) Me interesa leer

[Target answer: B) Me encanta leer]

[Explanation: Encantar expresses intense liking/passion.]

[Item 3: Dialogue Completion] Complete: "— Es muy caro. — _____"

[Target answer: Bueno, puedo bajar el precio / Le hago un descuento]

[Explanation: Logical response from seller offering a reduction.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Describe the layout and rooms of your home using "tener".
lessons.targe_language: sala, cocina, dormitorio, baño, habitaciones
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Welcome to Unit 9! Today you will learn how to describe the rooms and layout of your home.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Rooms: "la sala" (living room), "la cocina" (kitchen), "el dormitorio" (bedroom), "el baño" (bathroom).

[Bubble Type: Example] Mi casa tiene tres dormitorios, una cocina grande y dos baños.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "My house has three bedrooms"

[Target answer: Mi casa tiene tres dormitorios]

[Explanation: Dormitorio or habitación means bedroom.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "Cocino la comida en la _____." (kitchen)

[Target answer: cocina]

[Explanation: La cocina is the kitchen.]

[Item 3: Multiple Choice] Which room has a shower? A) El dormitorio B) El baño C) La sala

[Target answer: B) El baño]

[Explanation: El baño is the bathroom.]

lessons.lesson_name: El sofá está al lado de la ventana
lessons.learning_objectives: Describe furniture placement using prepositions of place.
lessons.targe_language: sofá, mesa, ventana, cama, silla, detrás de, entre
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Learn how to describe where furniture is positioned in a room.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Use "está" + preposition: "al lado de" (next to), "detrás de" (behind), "entre" (between).

[Bubble Type: Example] El sofá está al lado de la ventana y la mesa está en el centro.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "The sofa is next to the window"

[Target answer: El sofá está al lado de la ventana]

[Explanation: al lado de means next to.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "La silla está _____ de la mesa." (behind)

[Target answer: detrás]

[Explanation: detrás de means behind.]

[Item 3: Sentence Building] Arrange: "la ventana / está / La cama / junto a"

[Target answer: La cama está junto a la ventana]

[Explanation: Subject + verb + prepositional phrase.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Talk about household chores and obligations using "tener que".
lessons.targe_language: limpiar, lavar la ropa, cocinar, ordenar, pasar la aspiradora
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Learn how to discuss household chores and weekend responsibilities.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Use "Tengo que [infinitive]" (I have to...): "limpiar" (clean), "lavar la ropa" (do laundry).

[Bubble Type: Example] El fin de semana tengo que limpiar la casa y lavar la ropa.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "I have to clean the kitchen"

[Target answer: Tengo que limpiar la cocina]

[Explanation: Tengo que + infinitive verb expresses chore duty.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "Hoy me toca _____ la ropa." (wash)

[Target answer: lavar]

[Explanation: Lavar la ropa means wash clothes / do laundry.]

[Item 3: Multiple Choice] "I have to tidy my room": A) Tengo ordenar mi habitación B) Tengo que ordenar mi habitación C) Estoy ordenar mi habitación

[Target answer: B) Tengo que ordenar mi habitación]

[Explanation: Tener MUST be followed by 'que' for obligation.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Describe building floors and addresses using ordinal numbers.
lessons.targe_language: primer piso, segundo piso, tercer piso, edificio, ascensor
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Today you'll learn ordinal numbers to tell someone which floor you live on.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Ordinals: "primer" (1st), "segundo" (2nd), "tercer" (3rd), "cuarto" (4th). Note: primero/tercero drop -o before masculine nouns!

[Bubble Type: Example] Vivo en el primer piso de un edificio con ascensor.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "I live on the second floor"

[Target answer: Vivo en el segundo piso]

[Explanation: Segundo piso means second floor.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "Mi departamento está en el _____ (first) piso."

[Target answer: primer]

[Explanation: Primero shortens to 'primer' before singular masculine noun 'piso'.]

[Item 3: Multiple Choice] "Third floor": A) Tercero piso B) Tercer piso C) Tres piso

[Target answer: B) Tercer piso]

[Explanation: Tercero becomes 'tercer' before 'piso'.]

lessons.lesson_name: Repaso: Mi casa y mi barrio
lessons.learning_objectives: Give a cohesive description of your home, layout, furniture, and chores.
lessons.targe_language: review of home & ordinal vocabulary
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Congratulations! You reached the final review lesson of Level 2. Let's describe your complete home.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Summary: "Mi casa tiene...", "El sofá está...", "Tengo que limpiar...", and "Vivo en el segundo piso".

[Bubble Type: Example] Vivo en el segundo piso. Mi casa tiene tres habitaciones y hoy tengo que limpiar la cocina.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Fill in the blank] "Vivo en el _____ piso y mi casa _____ tres habitaciones."

[Target answer: primer, tiene]

[Explanation: primer piso = 1st floor, tiene = has.]

[Item 2: Multiple Choice] Express having to do chores: A) Tengo que limpiar B) Soy limpiar C) Quiero piso

[Target answer: A) Tengo que limpiar]

[Explanation: Tener que + infinitive for obligations.]

[Item 3: Dialogue Completion] Complete: "— ¿En qué piso vives? — _____"

[Target answer: Vivo en el segundo piso / Vivo en el tercer piso]

[Explanation: State your floor location with ordinal number.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Describe your profession and daily workplace duties.
lessons.targe_language: dedicarse a, encargarse de, el jefe, la empresa, puesto
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Welcome to Level 3 (B1)! Today you'll learn to discuss your profession and main job responsibilities.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Use "Me dedico a [field/verb]" (I work in...) and "Me encargo de [task]" (I am in charge of...).

[Bubble Type: Example] Me dedico al marketing y me encargo de gestionar las redes sociales.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "What do you do for a living?"

[Target answer: ¿A qué te dedicas?]

[Explanation: ¿A qué te dedicas? is standard for asking one's profession.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "Me _____ de organizar las reuniones." (am in charge of)

[Target answer: encargo]

[Explanation: Encargarse de means to be in charge of.]

[Item 3: Multiple Choice] "I work in education": A) Me dedico a la educación B) Me encargo la educación C) Vivo la educación

[Target answer: A) Me dedico a la educación]

[Explanation: Dedicarse a specifies professional field.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Talk about work history and experience using the Present Perfect.
lessons.targe_language: he trabajado, ha estudiado, experiencia laboral, el currículum
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Learn how to present your work history during job networking or interview settings.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Combine "he/ha trabajado" with duration: "He trabajado en esta empresa por dos años".

[Bubble Type: Example] He trabajado como ingeniero durante cinco años en Madrid.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "I have worked here for two years"

[Target answer: He trabajado aquí dos años]

[Explanation: He trabajado is Present Perfect for past work duration.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "Ella _____ trabajado en varias empresas." (has)

[Target answer: ha]

[Explanation: 'ha' pairs with ella.]

[Item 3: Sentence Building] Arrange: "tres / He / aquí / trabajado / años"

[Target answer: He trabajado aquí tres años]

[Explanation: Auxiliary + participle + adverbial duration.]

lessons.lesson_name: Llevo tres años en esta empresa
lessons.learning_objectives: Express duration of ongoing jobs or situations using "llevar".
lessons.targe_language: llevo... en, llevo... trabajando, la empresa, el cargo
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Learn a natural Spanish structure to state how long you've been working at a company.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Use "Llevo [time] en [place]" or "Llevo [time] trabajando" (I have been working for...).

[Bubble Type: Example] Llevo tres años trabajando en esta empresa.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "I've been at this company for 3 years"

[Target answer: Llevo tres años en esta empresa]

[Explanation: Llevar + time + en indicates ongoing duration.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "_____ dos años trabajando como gerente." (I have been)

[Target answer: Llevo]

[Explanation: Llevo + time + gerund indicates ongoing activity.]

[Item 3: Multiple Choice] "She has been here for 5 years": A) Lleva cinco años aquí B) Tiene cinco años aquí C) Es cinco años aquí

[Target answer: A) Lleva cinco años aquí]

[Explanation: Llevar indicates ongoing time duration.]

lessons.lesson_name: El año que viene buscaré otro trabajo
lessons.learning_objectives:
Express future career plans and professional goals using the Simple Future.

[Target answer: buscaré un nuevo trabajo]
lessons.targe_language: buscaré, ascenderé, cambiaré, el año que viene, meta profesional
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Learn how to express your long-term career goals using the Simple Future tense.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Regular -ar/-er/-ir verbs add -é (yo), -á (él/ella) to the infinitive: "buscaré" (I will search).

[Bubble Type: Example] El año que viene buscaré un nuevo trabajo y ascenderé.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "Next year I will look for a job"

[Target answer: El año que viene buscaré trabajo]

[Explanation: Buscaré is the simple future 'yo' form of buscar.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "El próximo mes _____ de puesto." (I will change)

[Target answer: cambiaré]

[Explanation: Cambiaré is simple future for 'yo'.]

[Item 3: Multiple Choice] "She will promote": A) Ascenderé B) Ascenderá C) Ascenderán

[Target answer: B) Ascenderá]

[Explanation: Ascenderá matches ella/él/usted in simple future.]

lessons.lesson_name: Tengo una reunión a las diez
lessons.learning_objectives: Coordinate meeting times, agendas, and deadlines with colleagues.
lessons.targe_language: reunión, la agenda, el plazo, el informe, convocar
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Learn essential workplace terminology for scheduling meetings and managing project deadlines.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Key terms: "la reunión" (meeting), "el plazo" (deadline), "el informe" (report).

[Bubble Type: Example] Tengo una reunión a las diez para presentar el informe.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "I have a meeting at ten"

[Target answer: Tengo una reunión a las diez]

[Explanation: Reunión = meeting.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "El _____ de este proyecto es el viernes." (deadline)

[Target answer: plazo]

[Explanation: El plazo means the deadline or time limit.]

[Item 3: Dialogue Completion] Complete: "— ¿A qué hora es la reunión? — _____"

[Target answer: Es a las diez / La reunión es a las tres]

[Explanation: State meeting time using Es a las + hour.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Present a complete career trajectory covering present role, history, and future goals.
lessons.targe_language: review of professional vocabulary
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Welcome to Unit 1 Review! Practice giving a professional self-introduction.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Summary: "Me dedico a...", "Llevo... años trabajando", and "En el futuro buscaré...".

[Bubble Type: Example] Me dedico al desarrollo de software. Llevo dos años en esta empresa y pronto ascenderé.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Fill in the blank] "Me _____ al diseño y _____ dos años en este puesto."

[Target answer: dedico, llevo]

[Explanation: dedico for profession field, llevo for duration.]

[Item 2: Multiple Choice] Ask about someone's job: A) ¿A qué te dedicas? B) ¿Dónde trabajaste? C) ¿Cuándo es la reunión?

[Target answer: A) ¿A qué te dedicas?]

[Explanation: Standard profession inquiry.]

[Item 3: Dialogue Completion] Complete: "— ¿Cuándo entregas el informe? — _____"

[Target answer: Mañana a las diez / El viernes es el plazo]

[Explanation: Answer addressing report deadline/time.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Express personal opinions clearly using "creo que" and "pienso que" + indicative.
lessons.targe_language: creo que, pienso que, opino que, en mi opinión, para mí
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Welcome to Unit 2! Today you'll learn how to share your perspective in discussions.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Use "Creo que..." or "Pienso que..." followed by regular Indicative verbs.

[Bubble Type: Example] Creo que esta idea es muy buena para el proyecto.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "I think that it is important"

[Target answer: Creo que es importante]

[Explanation: Creo que takes indicative verb forms.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "_____ que este plan va a funcionar." (I think)

[Target answer: Pienso]

[Explanation: Pienso que means I think that.]

[Item 3: Sentence Building] Arrange: "es / que / Creo / difícil"

[Target answer: Creo que es difícil]

[Explanation: Opinion trigger + que + verb + adjective.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Express polite agreement or disagreement during discussions.
lessons.targe_language: estoy de acuerdo, no estoy de acuerdo, tienes razón, depende
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Learn how to respectfully agree or disagree with someone's viewpoint in Spanish.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Say "Estoy de acuerdo" (I agree) or "No estoy de acuerdo" (I disagree). Add "Tienes razón" (You're right).

[Bubble Type: Example] Entiendo tu punto, pero no estoy de acuerdo contigo.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "I disagree"

[Target answer: No estoy de acuerdo]

[Explanation: No estoy de acuerdo expresses disagreement.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "Sí, _____ razón en ese punto." (you have)

[Target answer: tienes]

[Explanation: Tienes razón means you are right.]

[Item 3: Multiple Choice] How to politely agree? A) No estoy de acuerdo B) Estoy de acuerdo C) No me importa

[Target answer: B) Estoy de acuerdo]

[Explanation: Estoy de acuerdo means I agree.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Use impersonal expressions ("Es importante que...") trigger Present Subjunctive.
lessons.targe_language: es importante que, es necesario que, es mejor que, estudies, hagas
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Today you'll enter the Subjunctive mood! Learn how impersonal expressions trigger it.

[Bubble Type: Teaching] "Es importante que..." + Subjunctive ("estudies", "hagas"). Verb endings flip (-ar -> -e, -er/-ir -> -a)!

[Bubble Type: Example] Es importante que hables español todos los días.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Translation] Translate "It is important that you study"

[Target answer: Es importante que estudies]

[Explanation: Es importante que requires Present Subjunctive.]

[Item 2: Fill in the blank] "Es necesario que tú _____ temprano." (arrive - llegar)

[Target answer: llegues]

[Explanation: Llegues is Present Subjunctive for llegar.]

[Item 3: Multiple Choice] "It is better that you do it": A) Es mejor que lo haces B) Es mejor que lo hagas C) Es mejor que lo hiciste

[Target answer: B) Es mejor que lo hagas]

[Explanation: Hagas is the Subjunctive form of hacer.]

lessons.learning_objectives: Contrast positive belief (Indicative) vs negative belief (Subjunctive).
lessons.targe_language: no creo que, no pienso que, sea, vaya, tenga
lessons.phase_1:
[Bubble Type: Introduction] Learn a crucial Subjunctive rule: Positive opinions use Indicative, negative opinions use Subjunctive!

[Bubble Type: Teaching] Positive: "Creo que es verdad" (Indicative). Negative: "No creo que sea verdad" (Subjunctive - sea).

[Bubble Type: Example] No creo que el examen sea tan difícil.
lessons.phase_2:
[Item 1: Fill in the blank] "Creo que él _____ (is) honesto, pero no creo que _____ (be) fácil."

[Target answer: es, sea]

[Explanation: Indicative 'es' for positive belief, Subjunctive 'sea' for negative.]

[Item 2: Translation] Translate "I don't think that it is true"

[Target answer: No creo que sea verdad]

[Explanation: No creo que triggers Subjunctive 'sea'.]
